caption: Longitudinal transvaginal ultrasound demonstrates normal appearance of the uterus, including endometrium ﬅ, myometrium ﬆ, cervix ﬇, and cul-de-sac ﬈. The endovaginal probe is positioned within the anterior vaginal fornix ﬉. By convention, the left side of the image is anterior, and the right is posterior.
Transverse transvaginal ultrasound demonstrates normal appearance of the uterus, including endometrium ﬅ and myometrium ﬆ.

Longitudinal transabdominal ultrasound shows the uterus ﬅ, vagina ﬆ, and urinary bladder ﬇. Transabdominal ultrasound offers a larger field of view but less resolution compared to transvaginal ultrasound.
Transvaginal ultrasound shows a normal ovary ﬅ with few small follicles ﬆ and adjacent bowel ﬇.

This image demonstrates the different types of probes used in gynecologic ultrasound: 2D endovaginal probe ﬉, 3D endovaginal probe ﬅ, 3D curved transabdominal probe ﬈, 2D curved transabdominal probe ﬆ, 2D sector probe ﬊, 2D linear probe ﬇.
M- mode ultrasound in a 1st- trimester pregnancy shows embryonic cardiac activity ﬉, confirming viability of the gestation ﬅ. M-mode is typically used in obstetric ultrasound imaging.
Transverse transvaginal color Doppler evaluation shows color flow within the right ovary ﬆ with corresponding low-resistance spectral arterial waveform ﬅ. Note the normal dominant follicle ﬇.
Transverse transvaginal color Doppler evaluation shows color flow within the left ovarian stroma ﬆ with nonpulsatile spectral venous waveform ﬅ.
Longitudinal transabdominal ultrasound shows a complex, cystic adnexal mass ﬆ. Power Doppler evaluation demonstrates blood flow within a heterogeneous mural nodule ﬅ.

Sagittal transvaginal ultrasound shows a postmenopausal uterus with pencil-thin, echogenic atrophic endometrium ﬇.

Sagittal transvaginal ultrasound shows an anteverted uterus with thin endometrium and cystic changes ﬅ in the lower uterine segment, compatible with cystic atrophy in this patient undergoing tamoxifen therapy.
Axial 3D ultrasound shows 2 widely divergent uterine horns ﬅ, each with echogenic endometrium ﬆ.
Axial transabdominal ultrasound in a 24-year-old woman who presented with pelvic pain shows 2 widely divergent uterine horns ﬅ, each with echogenic endometrium ﬇. The 2 separate cervices ﬆ are noted.
Axial transabdominal pelvic ultrasound shows 2 widely separated uterine horns ﬅ with a gestational sac containing an embryo ﬇ within the right uterine horn.
Sagittal transabdominal ultrasound in a 23-year-old woman during routine obstetric imaging shows a fetal head ﬅ and an echogenic mass ﬇ separate from the gravid uterus.
Sagittal transabdominal ultrasound in the same patient shows the echogenic pelvic mass ﬅ. This was thought to represent an ovarian mass, possibly a mature cystic teratoma.
Coronal 3D ultrasound shows a septate uterus. The outer fundal contour is slightly concave with a shallow cleft (< 1 cm) ﬅ. There is an incomplete septum ﬇ extending to the lower uterine segment.
3D ultrasound in the same patient after catheter removal shows the endometrial synechia ﬅ.
Longitudinal transvaginal ultrasound shows fluid within the endometrial cavity with bridging synechiae ﬅ.
Transverse transvaginal ultrasound in the same patient shows fluid within the endometrial cavity with bridging synechiae ﬅ, which were proven on subsequent hysteroscopy.
Longitudinal transvaginal US in the same patient shows hyperechoic foci with shadowing within the endometrial cavity, corresponding to gas ﬅ.
Transverse transvaginal US in the same patient with endometritis shows echogenic foci with shadowing in the endometrial cavity corresponding to gas ﬅ.
Transverse transvaginal US demonstrates endometrial thickening ﬅ and echogenic foci with shadowing ﬆ, corresponding to foci of gas in this patient with endometritis.

Transverse color Doppler US of the uterus in the same patient shows hyperemia within the myometrium adjacent to the thickened endometrium ﬅ, which is not hypervascular. Polymicrobial infection was found on culture.
Ultrasound in the same patient demonstrates a large, echogenic uterine mass ﬅ with internal hyperechoic foci producing "dirty" shadowing ﬆ, which represent locules of gas.
Transabdominal pelvic ultrasound shows large intramural ﬅ and subserosal ﬇ leiomyomas arising from the uterine corpus that are isoechoic to the background myometrium.
Transverse transabdominal pelvic ultrasound in the same patient shows a large echogenic mass ﬅ within the central uterus with extensive posterior acoustic shadowing ﬇.
Sagittal transvaginal ultrasound in a patient with dysfunctional uterine bleeding shows a sharply marginated hypoechoic mass ﬅ in the endometrial cavity consistent with submucosal leiomyoma.
3D ultrasound reconstruction in the same patient shows a hypoechoic mass ﬅ in the fundal aspect of the endometrial echo complex, consistent with submucosal leiomyoma.
Transverse transvaginal ultrasound in a patient with dysfunctional uterine bleeding shows a large mass ﬅ distorting the endometrial echo complex ﬇ that is isoechoic to the background myometrium.

Sagittal transabdominal ultrasound in a patient with chronic pelvic pain and dysfunctional uterine bleeding shows multiple hypoechoic masses ﬅ of variable size arising from the uterus. Precise anatomic localization is somewhat limited due to technical factors.
Longitudinal transabdominal ultrasound shows a large, cystic mass in the central pelvis ﬇ containing complex internal septations. There was limited visualization of the uterine corpus and ovaries.

Longitudinal transabdominal ultrasound in the same patient shows an echogenic mass arising from the uterine fundus ﬅ with dense posterior acoustic shadowing, consistent with calcific degeneration of a leiomyoma.
Longitudinal transabdominal ultrasound shows an anechoic pedunculated mass ﬅ arising from the anterior uterus ﬇, consistent with cystic degeneration of a leiomyoma.
Longitudinal transvaginal ultrasound shows diffusely increased echogenicity ﬅ throughout the uterine corpus with "dirty" shadowing ﬇.
Longitudinal transabdominal pelvic ultrasound shows a large, heterogeneous mass ﬅ expanding the cervix, consistent with cervical leiomyoma.
Longitudinal transabdominal ultrasound in a patient with acute pelvic pain shows a large mass arising from the endometrium ﬅ that expands the cervix ﬇.
Transverse transabdominal color Doppler ultrasound in a patient with sudden-onset pelvic pain shows a heterogeneous, hypovascular solid and cystic mass ﬅ arising from the anterior uterus.

Transverse color Doppler ultrasound shows a heterogeneously hypoechoic uterine leiomyoma ﬅ contiguous with a tubular periuterine structure with similar characteristics and associated vascularity, representing extension into a periuterine vein ﬆ.
Longitudinal color Doppler ultrasound in the same patient shows a periuterine vein expanded by tumor thrombus ﬅ, which has internal vascularity ﬆ.
Transverse ultrasound of the uterus shows an echogenic mass that replaces the uterine myometrium ﬅ.
Longitudinal ultrasound of the uterus in the same patient demonstrates a large, echogenic mass with posterior acoustic shadowing ﬅ. Pathology confirmed lipoleiomyoma.
Transverse transvaginal ultrasound in a patient with uterine lipoleiomyoma shows a hyperechoic uterine fundal mass with posterior shadowing ﬅ.
Longitudinal transvaginal ultrasound in the same patient shows the hyperechoic mass with posterior acoustic shadowing ﬅ.
Longitudinal transvaginal ultrasound in the same patient shows focal, echogenic thickening of the endometrial echo complex ﬅ that is suggestive of, but not definitive for, polyp.

Longitudinal sonohysterogram in the same patient shows a broad-based polypoid mass ﬅ arising from the fundal aspect of the endometrial cavity, confirming the presence of polyp. Doppler interrogation shows mild internal vascularity.
Longitudinal transvaginal ultrasound shows diffuse, nonspecific thickening of the endometrial echo complex ﬅ.
Longitudinal sonohysterogram in the same patient shows fluid surrounding a fibrovascular stalk ﬅ in a pedunculated endometrial polyp ﬇ that was inapparent on conventional transvaginal images.
Longitudinal transabdominal ultrasound shows diffuse thickening of the endometrial echo complex ﬅ.
Transverse ultrasound in the same patient again shows diffuse thickening of the endometrial echo complex ﬅ. Differential includes polyp, endometrial hyperplasia, or endometrial carcinoma.
Longitudinal transvaginal sonohysterogram in the same patient shows a broad-based polyp ﬅ arising from the fundal aspect of the endometrium.

Longitudinal transvaginal ultrasound with color Doppler interrogation was performed in a patient with dysfunctional uterine bleeding. The endometrial echo complex was normal in double thickness and without evidence of abnormal vascularity.

Longitudinal transvaginal ultrasound with color Doppler in the same patient revealed an ovoid echogenic structure ﬅ with avid color Doppler flow expanding the endocervical canal, consistent with endocervical polyp.
3D ultrasound of the uterine corpus in the same patient shows an echogenic polypoid mass ﬅ within the central endometrial cavity, consistent with endometrial polyp.
Longitudinal transvaginal ultrasound (TVUS) shows diffuse thickening of the endometrial echo complex ﬅ, measuring up to 20 mm in double thickness.
Longitudinal TVUS with color Doppler in the same patient shows typically avascular appearance of endometrial hyperplasia ﬅ.
Longitudinal TVUS of the uterus shows focal thickening of the endometrium ﬅ with tiny anechoic cystic spaces ﬇. Note the thin lower stripe ﬈.

Transverse TVUS in the same patient at the level of the thickened cystic endometrium ﬅ has the typical Swiss cheese appearance of endometrial hyperplasia. The findings of focal hyperplasia overlap with endometrial polyps and cancer. Endometrial biopsy is required to establish a definitive diagnosis.
Longitudinal TVUS in a patient with menorrhagia shows marked thickening of the endometrial echo complex ﬅ, measuring 28 mm in double thickness.
Longitudinal TVUS shows focal thickening of the endometrial echo complex ﬅ at 21 mm in double thickness with tapering to normal-appearing endometrium ﬇.
Longitudinal TVUS in the same patient shows diffuse Swiss cheese-appearing cystic thickening of the endometrial echo complex ﬅ.

Longitudinal transvaginal ultrasound does not clearly demonstrate the endometrial stripe. Poor visualization of the endometrial echo complex in the setting of vaginal bleeding is nondiagnostic and should be further evaluated.
Transverse color Doppler transvaginal ultrasound shows a large, irregular mass ﬅ along the endometrium with blood/debris ﬆ in the endometrial canal.
Transvaginal ultrasound of the uterus in the same patient shows a large, solid, echogenic mass ﬅ.
Longitudinal transvaginal ultrasound shows an echogenic mass with small cystic spaces ﬆ expanding the endometrial cavity ﬅ. Resection proved this to be a carcinosarcoma.
Transverse transvaginal ultrasound with color Doppler in the same patient shows the echogenic mass expanding the endometrial cavity ﬅ with associated internal vascularity.
Longitudinal ultrasound shows a large, heterogeneous, echogenic mass with regions of cystic change expanding the endometrial cavity ﬅ. Resection proved this mass to be carcinosarcoma.

Transverse ultrasound in the same patient centered at the cervix shows the large, heterogeneous, intracavitary echogenic mass ﬅ with regions of cystic change ﬆ prolapsing and expanding the endocervical canal.
Sagittal transvaginal ultrasound shows an ill-defined area of decreased myometrial echogenicity ﬅ, resulting in a spongy myometrial echotexture.

Sagittal transvaginal ultrasound with color Doppler in the same patient shows a markedly hypervascular focus ﬅ corresponding to the spongy area on the grayscale image. The juxtaposition of red and blue is typical of flow reversal in an AVM.
Sagittal transvaginal ultrasound with pulsed Doppler in the same patient shows characteristic high- flow, low-resistance arterial waveform in a uterine AVM.
Transverse transvaginal ultrasound shows an ill- defined area of small anechoic spaces within the myometrium ﬅ, producing spongy myometrial echotexture.

Sagittal transvaginal ultrasound with color Doppler in the same patient shows marked vascular flow within the myometrium ﬅ corresponding to the spongy myometrium in the grayscale image, classic features of uterine AVM.

Transvaginal ultrasound with color Doppler in a patient with menometrorrhagia shows a serpiginous area of mosaic Doppler signal ﬅ adjacent to the endometrial echo complex, consistent with iatrogenic uterine AVM.

Transvaginal transverse ultrasound with color Doppler in a patient with a history of prior uterine trauma and instrumentation shows a large area of marked blood flow with aliasing in the myometrium ﬅ, consistent with large uterine AVM.
Longitudinal transabdominal US shows heterogeneous uterine enlargement with a dominant intramural leiomyoma ﬅ in the proximal uterine corpus.

Longitudinal transabdominal US of the same patient 2 years following embolization shows significant atrophy of the dominant leiomyoma ﬅ. Dense, peripheral calcifications are seen, a.k.a. the fetal head sign.
Transverse color Doppler ultrasound shows diffuse thickening of the endometrial echo complex ﬅ with multiple anechoic cysts in a patient on tamoxifen.
Transvaginal ultrasound in the same patient shows a large, anechoic cyst arising from the right ovary.

Longitudinal transvaginal ultrasound with color Doppler in a patient on tamoxifen shows diffuse, homogeneous thickening of the endometrium ﬅ. No abnormal vascularity is seen within the endometrium to suggest the presence of a polyp.
Longitudinal transvaginal ultrasound shows cystic changes throughout the endometrial echo complex ﬅ in a patient undergoing tamoxifen therapy.
Transverse transvaginal ultrasound in the same patient again shows diffuse cystic changes throughout a mildly thickened endometrial echo complex ﬅ.
Sagittal transvaginal ultrasound in a patient receiving tamoxifen shows diffuse thickening of the endometrial echo complex ﬅ with scattered cysts.

Transverse transabdominal ultrasound shows marked, heterogeneous thickening of the endometrial echo complex ﬅ, concerning for endometrial carcinoma. However, endometrial biopsy revealed endometrial hyperplasia.

Transverse transvaginal ultrasound in the same patient revealed a prominent leiomyoma ﬅ with cystic degeneration ﬆ arising from the lower uterine segment that had rapidly enlarged since initiating tamoxifen therapy.

Sagittal transvaginal ultrasound with color Doppler in a patient receiving tamoxifen shows that focal thickening of the endometrial echo complex ﬅ has associated vascularity, suggestive of endometrial polyp.
Transverse transvaginal ultrasound in the same patient shows an intramural leiomyoma ﬅ arising from the right aspect of the uterine fundus that had enlarged since the onset of tamoxifen therapy.
3D ultrasound reconstruction of the uterine corpus in the same patient again shows an intramural leiomyoma ﬅ and an endometrial polyp ﬆ to better advantage in a patient undergoing tamoxifen therapy.
Transverse transvaginal ultrasound in the same patient shows an enlarged, mildly complex, septated cyst arising from the right ovary.

Transverse transvaginal ultrasound with color Doppler in the same patient shows a heterogeneous, multilobular mass expanding the endometrial cavity ﬅ with internal vascularity. Endometrial biopsy revealed the presence of endometrial carcinoma.
Longitudinal transvaginal US shows a linear shadowing structure ﬇ in the central uterine cavity. An echogenic focus is noted in the fundus that is thought to represent the arm of the IUD ﬅ.
3D US in the same patient confirms appropriate positioning of the stem ﬇ and arms ﬅ of the IUD within the central endometrial cavity.

Longitudinal transvaginal US shows a linear echogenic structure ﬇ within the lower uterine segment and endocervical canal that appears to represent a low- lying IUD, although the arms of the device could not be definitively seen by 2D technique.
3D US in the same patient confirms a low- lying, malpositioned IUD with the stem in the endocervical canal ﬊ and the arms obliquely oriented within the lower uterine segment ﬅ.

Longitudinal transvaginal US in a patient with dyspareunia shows a malpositioned IUD with the echogenic arms of the device ﬅ within the lower uterine segment and endocervical canal. The stem was poorly visualized on this exam.

Longitudinal transvaginal ultrasound in a patient with remote cesarean delivery shows focal thinning of the myometrium of the anterior lower uterine segment with posterior acoustic shadowing ﬅ. Fluid fills the defect ﬇.
Transverse transvaginal ultrasound in the same patient shows the fluid-filled cesarean scar defect ﬇. The length ﬆ of scar is measured side to side in the transverse plane.
Longitudinal transvaginal ultrasound in the same patient demonstrates the cesarean scar measurement technique for the width ﬅ and depth ﬇ of the scar, as well as the residual myometrial thickness ﬆ.
Transvaginal ultrasound in a patient with a history of remote cesarean delivery shows a triangular fluid collection ﬅ in the anterior lower uterine segment, consistent with cesarean scar niche.

Transvaginal ultrasound in a patient that had undergone recent cesarean section shows a complex fluid collection ﬅ along the anterior margin of the lower uterine segment, consistent with bladder flap hematoma.

Morphological Uterus Sonographic Assessment (MUSA) 2015 criteria for the diagnosis of adenomyosis is shown: (A) Asymmetrical thickening, (B) myometrial cysts, (C) fan-shaped shadowing, (D) echogenic subendometrial lines and buds, (E) hyperechoic islands, (F) translesional vascularity, (G) interrupted junctional zone, (H) irregular junctional zone. The definitions of these features can be found in the MUSA Consensus Opinion.
Sagittal transvaginal ultrasound shows a rain shower or Venetian blind appearance of the posterior myometrium ﬆ with a 4-mm myometrial cyst ﬇. The endometrium ﬅ is obscured.
Transverse transvaginal ultrasound shows an enlarged, globular uterus ﬅ and myometrial heterogeneity without a focal mass. The normal smooth external contour of the uterus is maintained.

Transverse color Doppler ultrasound of the uterus in the same patient shows increased vascularity with a random speckled pattern of flow in the anterior wall of the uterus ﬅ, typical of adenomyosis. This is in contrast to the peripheral vascular pattern seen with leiomyomas.
Sagittal transvaginal ultrasound in the same patient shows heterogeneous thickening of the anterior myometrium ﬅ with eccentric displacement of the endometrial echo complex ﬆ.
Sagittal color Doppler ultrasound of the uterus in the same patient shows an increased number of tortuous vessels throughout the affected myometrium ﬅ.

Longitudinal transvaginal ultrasound shows an ill-defined, hypoechoic intramural mass ﬇ arising from the uterine fundus. Punctate echogenic foci ﬅ are noted, consistent with hemorrhagic endometrial glands.

Sagittal transvaginal ultrasound shows a hypoechoic, ill-defined, heterogeneous mass ﬅ. An anechoic myometrial cyst is noted within the periphery of the mass. Characteristic "Venetian blind" shadows ﬆ are likewise seen throughout the mass.
Longitudinal transabdominal Doppler ultrasound of the uterus shows increased density of tortuous, penetrating vessels within an adenomyoma ﬅ.
Longitudinal transvaginal ultrasound shows a complex intramural lesion ﬅ in the left uterine fundus that is centrally hypoechoic with a rim of increased echogenicity.
Axial color Doppler ultrasound shows a centrally echogenic mass ﬅ, consistent with intralesional hemorrhage. A mildly vascular hypoechoic rim is noted.
Longitudinal transvaginal ultrasound shows a pedunculated isoechoic lesion extending into the endocervical canal ﬅ.
Transverse transvaginal ultrasound with color Doppler in the same patient shows the pedunculated lesion in the endocervical canal has a vascular stalk ﬅ. This was a biopsy-proven endocervical polyp.
Longitudinal transvaginal ultrasound shows an echogenic pedunculated mass within the endocervical canal ﬅ with small internal cystic regions ﬆ.
Transverse color Doppler ultrasound in the same patient shows internal vascularity ﬅ within the polypoid endocervical mass. This was biopsy-proven endocervical polyp.
Longitudinal transvaginal ultrasound shows a pedunculated endocervical polyp ﬅ surrounded with fluid ﬆ.
Transverse color Doppler transvaginal ultrasound in the same patient shows linear vascularity within the vascular stalk ﬆ of the pedunculated endocervical polyp ﬅ.

Longitudinal transvaginal ultrasound in the same patient shows the probe in the anterior vaginal fornix abutting the anterior cervical leiomyoma ﬅ, which is circumscribed, heterogeneous, and hypo-/isoechoic to myometrium.
Transverse transvaginal ultrasound in the same patient shows the anterior cervical leiomyoma ﬅ, which is heterogeneously hypo- /isoechoic to myometrium and demonstrates vascularity on color Doppler.
Longitudinal transvaginal ultrasound shows a hypoechoic, pedunculated cervical leiomyoma ﬅ expanding the endocervical canal, which was surgically resected.

Transverse transvaginal ultrasound in the same patient shows the pedunculated cervical leiomyoma replacing the endocervical cavity ﬅ. There are central hypoechoic foci ﬆ corresponding to regions of degeneration.
Transvaginal ultrasound shows the lower uterine segment ﬅ immediately adjacent to the probe in the vaginal vault, consistent with prior trachelectomy.
Sagittal transvaginal ultrasound shows a thickened endocervical mucosa ﬅ. The hypoechoic areas ﬆ represent tiny cysts within the mucosa. There is a sliver of fluid in the endocervical canal.
Longitudinal transvaginal ultrasound with color Doppler shows heterogeneous, predominantly hypoechoic, avascular thickening of the inner layer of the cervix ﬅ.

Longitudinal transvaginal ultrasound shows scattered, partially coalescent foci ﬅ arising from the inner epithelial layer of the cervix, consistent with increased mucin content within hyperplastic cervical glands.
Axial transvaginal ultrasound shows an ovoid cyst with low-level echoes ﬅ and posterior acoustic shadowing ﬇ in the cervix. Complicated nabothian cysts may have proteinaceous contents.

Longitudinal color Doppler ultrasound in the same patient shows no internal blood flow in these simple cysts ﬅ. Note the superficial location of the cysts relative to the hypoechoic endocervical canal ﬇, a characteristic feature of nabothian cysts.
Transverse transvaginal ultrasound of the cervix shows anechoic cysts ﬅ surrounding the endocervical canal, consistent with nabothian cysts.
Longitudinal transvaginal ultrasound shows a very large, unilocular cystic lesion ﬅ arising from the cervix, containing low-level echoes that measure 3.1 cm.

Transverse transvaginal ultrasound in the same patient shows a hypoechoic lesion ﬅ adjacent to the endocervical canal ﬇. The lesion was felt to represent a hemorrhagic nabothian cyst given the presence of low-level echoes that was later confirmed by transvaginal biopsy.
Longitudinal transvaginal ultrasound with color Doppler in a postmenopausal patient shows a retroverted uterus with echogenic fluid distending the endometrial cavity, consistent with hematometra ﬅ.

Transverse transvaginal ultrasound in the same patient shows a distended endometrial cavity by echogenic fluid, consistent with hematometra ﬅ. Further work-up demonstrated cervical stenosis and excluded underlying malignancy.
Longitudinal transvaginal ultrasound in a patient with cervical stenosis demonstrates hydrometra ﬅ with distended endometrial and cervical cavities with relative caliber change near the cervical os.
Transverse transvaginal ultrasound in the same patient demonstrates hematometra ﬅ. Subsequent work-up excluded an underlying cervical malignancy.
Longitudinal color Doppler ultrasound in a patient with benign cervical stenosis shows fluid within the endometrial and endocervical cavity ﬅ.
Longitudinal transvaginal ultrasound in a patient with cervical stenosis shows distention of the cervical cavity with fluid containing low-level internal echoes ﬅ.
Longitudinal pelvic ultrasound shows marked distention of the vagina with blood products ﬅ.

Longitudinal transvaginal ultrasound in the same patient shows the upper vagina dilated by echogenic blood products ﬅ. The probe was inserted partway into the vagina, which was obstructed by a transverse septum.
Sagittal transvaginal color Doppler ultrasound shows a well-circumscribed, vascularized mass ﬅ. Smaller leiomyomas may be missed on transvaginal ultrasound if not clinically suspected.
Transvaginal color Doppler ultrasound in a 47- year-old woman who presented with vaginal bleeding shows a vascular vaginal mass ﬅ. The mass is homogeneously hypoechoic, typical of leiomyomas.
Transvaginal color Doppler ultrasound in a 42- year-old woman who presented with multiple vaginal lesions shows a large, vascular vaginal mass ﬅ indenting the urinary bladder ﬇.
Longitudinal grayscale ultrasound of the vulva demonstrates a lobular echogenic mass containing several echogenic nodules ﬅ.

Transverse color Doppler ultrasound of the vulva in the same patient demonstrates a lobulated echogenic mass ﬅ with large feeding vessel ﬆ and internal vascularity. This was proven to be a vulvar slow-flow vascular malformation on resection.
Longitudinal ultrasound in a 2-year-old girl with vaginal embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma shows a large, echogenic mass with small, hypoechoic foci filling the vagina ﬅ.
Transverse color Doppler ultrasound in the same patient shows vascularity within the vaginal mass ﬅ.
Axial translabial pelvic ultrasound in a 15-month-old girl shows a large, homogeneous vaginal mass ﬅ.
Translabial ultrasound shows a simple, anechoic vaginal cyst ﬈. The translabial approach can be used to visualize lower vaginal cysts.
Transvaginal US shows a horseshoe-shaped, heterogeneous structure ﬈ surrounding the urethra ﬅ. The heterogeneous echogenicity is due to debris.

Transperineal US shows a well-defined structure ﬅ at the external urethral meatus, which demonstrates uniform low-level echoes. The urethra is seen as a tubular anechoic structure ﬇ anterior to the vagina ﬆ.
Transverse transabdominal ultrasound of the pelvis in a 6-year-old girl demonstrates a vagina that is full of echogenic material with posterior acoustic shadowing ﬅ.
Longitudinal ultrasound of the pelvis in the same patient shows echogenic and shadowing material within the vagina ﬅ. This was laterally shown to be gravel and rocks.

Transverse ultrasound of the pelvis in a woman who presented with a stuck tampon after the string was broken off shows a curvilinear echogenic structure in the vaginal cavity with posterior acoustic shadowing ﬅ, corresponding to the lost tampon.
Longitudinal ultrasound in the same patient shows the curvilinear echogenic tampon ﬅ in the vaginal cavity with posterior acoustic shadowing ﬆ.

Transvaginal ultrasound in a 23-year-old woman shows a 5-cm, well-defined, anechoic ovarian cystic structure ﬅ. Note the curved line at the periphery of the larger cyst ﬇ representing cumulus oophorus.

Transvaginal ultrasound in a 34-year-old woman shows a 7-cm, well-defined, anechoic ovarian cystic structure ﬅ. Note the curved line at the periphery of the larger cyst ﬇ representing cumulus oophorus. The compressed ovarian parenchyma is seen at the periphery of the cyst ﬈.

Transvaginal ultrasound in a 27-year-old woman shows a 4-cm, well- defined, anechoic ovarian cystic structure ﬅ. Note the presence of 2 curved lines at the periphery of the cyst ﬇ representing cumulus oophorus.

Transvaginal ultrasound of the ovary demonstrates a thick-walled cyst ﬆ with a few low-level internal echoes ﬅ. In a premenopausal patient, this is most likely to be a normal corpus luteum cyst with a small amount of hemorrhage.
Transvaginal color Doppler ultrasound in the same patient demonstrates prominent vascularity ﬆ about the periphery of the cyst, the so- called ring of fire appearance of a corpus luteum.

Transvaginal ultrasound demonstrates a subtle, solid- appearing ovarian mass ﬆ. Faint posterior acoustic enhancement ﬅ is noted, a clue that this may represent a hemorrhagic or collapsed corpus luteum cyst.

Transvaginal color Doppler ultrasound of the ovary demonstrates the solid- appearing mass to be avascular with prominent peripheral vascular flow ﬆ, the so-called ring of fire appearance. In a premenopausal patient, this is consistent with a normal corpus luteum.

Transvaginal ultrasound of the pelvis in a premenopausal patient shows a thick-walled cyst ﬆ arising from the ovary, a typical appearance of a corpus luteum cyst. Note the increased echogenicity of the irregular cyst wall.

Transvaginal color Doppler ultrasound of the ovary in the same patient shows a classic ring of fire appearance of the corpus luteum, reflecting the increased vascularity of the cyst wall. Pulsed wave Doppler (not shown) demonstrated a low- resistance waveform.
Transvaginal color Doppler ultrasound shows a hemorrhagic cyst ﬇ with diffuse, increased echogenicity resembling a mature cystic teratoma. Follow-up ultrasound revealed complete resolution.

Transvaginal color Doppler ultrasound shows a hemorrhagic cyst ﬇ with fibrin strands creating a reticular pattern described as lace-like, fishnet, or cobweb appearance and a retracted avascular clot ﬅ. "Septations" are incomplete in contrast to septations within ovarian neoplasms.
Transvaginal color Doppler ultrasound shows a hemorrhagic cyst with a fine reticular meshwork of fibrin strands and a straight edge along the retracting clot ﬇.
Transvaginal color Doppler ultrasound shows a hemorrhagic cyst ﬇ with a retracted avascular clot ﬅ.
Transvaginal color Doppler ultrasound shows a fishnet appearance, a common appearance of hemorrhagic cyst.

Transvaginal color Doppler ultrasound shows a hemorrhagic corpus luteal cyst in a pregnant woman with pelvic pain. It is filled with low- level echoes ﬆ and has peripheral increased vascularity "ring of fire" ﬇. This can be confused with an ectopic pregnancy, but most ectopics are located in the fallopian tube and can be separated from the ovary by exerting gentle pressure with the probe.

Transvaginal ultrasound in the same patient shows low-level echoes with a slight reticular pattern typical of a hemorrhagic cyst ﬅ. Note the posterior acoustic enhancement ﬇. In the reproductive age group, hemorrhagic cysts with a classic appearance do not require follow-up unless > 5 cm.
Color Doppler ultrasound shows a classic fishnet appearance created by fibrinous strands ﬇. In addition, there is a retracting clot ﬆ adherent to the cyst wall.
Transvaginal ultrasound shows a typical case of a hemorrhagic cyst with fibrinous strands ﬇ and a retracting clot ﬆ.
Sagittal transvaginal ultrasound in the same patient shows the smooth edge of the retracting clot ﬇.
Transvaginal ultrasound shows an incomplete margin ﬆ of the right ovary in this woman who was in the emergency room with pelvic pain. Note the mildly echogenic surrounding free fluid ﬇.

Sagittal transvaginal ultrasound of the cul-de-sac in the same patient shows fluid that is more echogenic ﬇, the result of clot formation. Rupture of a hemorrhagic cyst can cause a hemoperitoneum. It is always important to look for echogenic free fluid in the cul- de-sac, Morrison pouch, and right upper quadrant.

Longitudinal transvaginal ultrasound in the same patient shows a small, simple cyst ﬉ arising from the right ovary ﬅ. When compared to prior studies, this had been unchanged for several years and was most consistent with an ovarian inclusion cyst.
Transverse transvaginal ultrasound in the same patient demonstrates a rounded, anechoic simple cyst ﬆ arising from the left ovary ﬅ. This is most likely to represent an ovarian inclusion cyst.
Longitudinal transabdominal ultrasound shows a hypoechoic cystic lesion (calipers) arising from the left ovary. Linear artifact ﬅ extending through the lesion prevents accurate characterization.
Longitudinal transvaginal ultrasound in the same patient demonstrates the left ovarian lesion (calipers) to be simple in appearance and likely to represent an ovarian inclusion cyst.

Transverse power Doppler ultrasound in the same patient demonstrates no internal flow within the cyst. A small, simple ovarian cyst in a postmenopausal patient is likely to represent an ovarian inclusion cyst.
Longitudinal transvaginal ultrasound shows a simple-appearing cyst ﬅ arising from the left ovary ﬆ.

Longitudinal transvaginal ultrasound in the same patient shows a rounded, anechoic, simple cyst ﬅ within the right ovary ﬆ, consistent with an inclusion cyst. Note the peripheral location of the cyst with the ovarian parenchyma.
Transverse transvaginal ultrasound shows a small, ovoid, simple-appearing left ovarian cyst ﬆ in this postmenopausal patient. The patient was asymptomatic.

Longitudinal transvaginal ultrasound shows a small, simple cyst ﬆ arising from the right ovary ﬅ. In postmenopausal patients, a small, simple cyst that remains stable in size and imaging appearance on follow-up is likely to represent an ovarian inclusion cyst.

Transvaginal color Doppler ultrasound in a 37- year-old woman shows an ovarian mixed cystic and solid mass ﬅ. The solid component is vascularized. The cystic components demonstrate low- level echoes.

Axial transabdominal ultrasound in a 69-year-old patient shows a predominantly solid, large adnexal mass ﬅ with areas of cystic change.

Axial transvaginal US in a 42-year-old woman who presented with a palpable mass shows a multilocular cystic adnexal lesion ﬅ with a prominent solid component ﬇.

Transvaginal US shows an ovarian cystic structure ﬅ containing an echogenic mural nodule (dermoid plug, Rokitansky nodule) ﬇ displaying posterior shadowing ﬈.
Sagittal transvaginal color Doppler US shows a diffusely echogenic ovarian mass ﬅ with no internal blood flow. The ovary contains 2 simple-appearing follicles ﬆ.

Axial transvaginal color Doppler US shows a highly echogenic mural nodule ﬇ with ill-defined posterior shadowing and a tip of the iceberg appearance within a less echogenic structure ﬅ containing uniform low-level echoes.

Axial transabdominal US shows another characteristic appearance of a dermoid cyst. There are numerous hyperechoic rounded structures ﬅ, 1-2 cm in diameter, floating in a hypoechoic fluid-containing cystic lesion ﬇.

Axial transvaginal US shows the characteristic dermoid plugs ﬅ appearing as echogenic mural nodules with ill-defined posterior shadowing. Fine linear echogenic shadows ﬇ are present in the cyst fluid, representing hair.
Axial transvaginal color Doppler US shows the characteristic dermoid mesh appearance due to multiple echogenic lines and dots caused by hair in the dermoid cyst.
Sagittal transvaginal US shows an ovarian dermoid cyst with dermoid plug ﬇, linear echogenic lines ﬅ due to intracystic hair, and a fat-fluid level ﬆ.

Axial transabdominal color Doppler ultrasound shows a heterogeneous ovarian mass ﬅ containing cystic changes ﬆ and areas of increased echogenicity with posterior shadowing ﬇ due to tumoral calcifications.
Axial transabdominal ultrasound shows a heterogeneous ovarian mass ﬅ containing areas of increased echogenicity ﬇ that may be due to fat or calcifications.

Axial transvaginal color Doppler US shows a solid ovarian mass ﬅ with slightly increased vascularity.

Axial transabdominal color Doppler US shows an ovarian mass ﬅ with increased vascularity in a radial distribution ﬇ within fibrovascular septa separating individual tumor lobules. This pattern of vascularized septa in a solid ovarian mass in a young patient is characteristic of dysgerminoma.

Transabdominal color Doppler ultrasound shows a solid adnexal mass ﬅ with moderate internal vascularity.

Axial transabdominal color Doppler ultrasound shows a predominantly solid right ovarian mass ﬅ with a multilocular, cystic component ﬇.
Axial transabdominal ultrasound shows a heterogeneous but predominantly solid right ovarian mass ﬅ with small, anechoic cysts ﬇.
Sagittal transvaginal ultrasound in a 33-year-old woman shows a right ovarian mass ﬅ that is predominantly solid but with numerous small, cystic spaces, exhibiting a Swiss cheese appearance.

The Swiss cheese appearance closely resembles that of benign hemorrhagic cyst, and these 2 entities can only be differentiated by the presence of septal blood flow in granulosa cell tumors (GCTs).
Transvaginal color Doppler ultrasound shows a hypovascular, hypoechoic ovarian mass ﬅ with significant posterior shadowing ﬇ masking the posterior wall.

Axial transabdominal color Doppler ultrasound in a 42-year-old woman who presented with pelvic pain shows a moderately vascular, solid left ovarian mass ﬅ. There is a central area of increased echogenicity ﬇.
Axial transvaginal ultrasound in a 34-year-old woman with a palpable adnexal mass shows a left ovarian mass ﬅ with solid ﬇ and cystic ﬆ components.

Transvaginal ultrasound in a 74-year-old woman who presented with a palpable adnexal mass shows a slightly hyperechoic left ovarian solid mass ﬅ.
Transvaginal duplex Doppler ultrasound in the same patient shows increased vascularity of the left ovarian mass ﬅ with low- resistance flow.
Transvaginal ultrasound in a 75-year-old woman who presented with increasing facial hair shows a small (1.8- cm) right ovarian mass ﬅ with homogeneous increased echogenicity.
Transvaginal power Doppler ultrasound in the same patient shows increased blood flow within the ovarian mass ﬅ. Pathology confirmed Sertoli- Leydig cell tumor.

Transvaginal ultrasound in a 19-year-old woman who presented with amenorrhea and acne shows a subtle right ovarian mass ﬅ that shows mild increased echogenicity relative to the normal ovary (calipers).

Axial transabdominal ultrasound shows a predominantly solid mass ﬅ with small, cleft-like cystic spaces ﬇.

Sagittal transvaginal color Doppler ultrasound in a 57-year-old woman with a history of rectal carcinoma shows a right ovarian mixed solid and cystic mass ﬅ with blood flow within the solid component.
Axial transabdominal color Doppler pelvic ultrasound in an 18-year-old woman shows an enlarged, hypovascular right ovary ﬅ. The ovary shows homogeneous low echogenicity without visible follicles.

Axial transabdominal color Doppler pelvic ultrasound in a 55-year-old woman who presented with palpable adnexal masses shows an enlarged right ovary ﬅ. The ovary shows homogeneous low echogenicity with 1 follicle ﬇ displaced toward the periphery.
Axial transabdominal pelvic ultrasound in the same patient shows an enlarged left ovary ﬅ. The ovary shows homogeneous low echogenicity with a small area of cystic change ﬇.
Transvaginal ultrasound shows a homogeneously hypoechoic mass with posterior acoustic enhancement ﬈, classic features of an endometrioma.
Transvaginal ultrasound shows a thick- walled mass arising from the ovary containing homogeneous, low-level echoes. Echogenic mural foci ﬅ are commonly seen in an endometrioma.

Transvaginal ultrasound shows a homogeneously hypoechoic adnexal mass ﬅ with posterior acoustic enhancement ﬈, typical features of an endometrioma. An echogenic mural nodule with comet-tail artifact ﬆ is also a characteristic feature of endometriomas.
Transvaginal ultrasound in the same patient again shows a right adnexal mass ﬅ containing low-level internal echoes, consistent with endometrioma.
Transvaginal ultrasound in the same patient shows a thick-walled mass ﬇ containing low-level internal echoes with posterior acoustic enhancement ﬅ, consistent with endometrioma.

Transabdominal ultrasound shows a thick- walled mass containing low- level internal echoes and posterior acoustic enhancement ﬈. Echogenic mural nodules ﬅ are likewise frequently seen in endometriomas.
Transabdominal ultrasound with color Doppler in the same patient demonstrates mural flow ﬅ. No internal color flow is seen in endometriomas.

Transabdominal ultrasound in the same patient several years later demonstrates interval enlargement of a right adnexal mass ﬅ measuring up to 8 cm. The mass was felt to represent an endometrioma despite the mildly heterogeneous variant internal echotexture.
Transabdominal ultrasound shows a thick- walled right adnexal mass containing a fluid-fluid level with a dependent echogenic layer ﬅ, generally indicative of recent internal hemorrhage.

Transvaginal ultrasound in the same patient again shows a thick-walled right adnexal mass, consistent with endometrioma. The internal heterogeneity ﬅ and fluid- fluid level ﬇ are less typical features of endometriomas.
Transvaginal ultrasound shows a hypoechoic right adnexal mass in a patient undergoing tamoxifen therapy. Scattered foci of increased echogenicity ﬅ are noted, an atypical finding in endometriomas.

Transvaginal ultrasound with color Doppler in the same patient shows color flow within the echogenic nodules ﬅ. Findings are most compatible with tamoxifen- related decidualization of an endometrioma given the clinical history although malignant transformation may present in a similar fashion.

Transabdominal ultrasound in the same patient shows a thick-walled mass with low- level internal echoes ﬇ and posterior acoustic enhancement ﬈, consistent with classic endometrioma. Small, echogenic mural nodules are noted ﬆ, concerning for malignant transformation. The lesion was consistent with ovarian endometrioid carcinoma following resection.

Transabdominal ultrasound in a gravid patient shows a classic endometrioma ﬅ. However, a smaller mass ﬇ is also noted containing nodular, polypoid internal elements, concerning for malignant transformation of an endometrioma.
Transvaginal ultrasound in a pregnant woman with known endometriosis shows a left adnexal hypoechoic mass with a prominent echogenic mural nodule ﬅ.

Transvaginal ultrasound with color Doppler in the same patient shows a right adnexal hypoechoic mass containing a vascular mural nodule ﬅ. Findings were consistent with pregnancy-related decidualized endometriomas, which may mimic ovarian malignancy.
Transabdominal ultrasound in the same patient shows a poorly marginated, heterogeneous mass ﬅ with ill-defined areas of decreased echogenicity ﬇ along the left anterolateral margin of the mass.

Transverse transabdominal US shows bilateral adnexal endometriomas ﬅ. Ill-defined, hypoechoic plaque ﬇ is noted between the uterus ﬈ and rectum ﬊, suspicious for deep infiltrating endometriosis (DIE).

Sagittal transvaginal US in a patient with chronic pelvic pain shows an ill-defined, hypoechoic plaque ﬅ in the rectouterine pouch with an associated negative uterine sliding sign.
Longitudinal transabdominal US shows a hypoechoic mass ﬅ with small, cystic foci in the posterior bladder wall that is separate from the uterus ﬆ.
Transabdominal US in a patient with chronic pelvic pain shows a right adnexal endometrioma ﬅ and an echogenic tubular structure ﬇ in the right rectouterine pouch.
Transverse transvaginal US shows bilateral adnexal masses ﬅ in close proximity to one another with tethering ﬇ of the adjacent posterior uterine serosa.
Transabdominal US in a patient with chronic pelvic pain shows a thick-walled, right ovarian mass ﬅ with homogeneous, low-level internal echoes, consistent with classic endometrioma.
Transabdominal color Doppler US in the same patient shows a multilobular left adnexal mass, likewise consistent with complex endometrioma.
Transabdominal US shows a hypoechoic, densely shadowing, poorly marginated mass within the anterior abdominal wall in a patient with a history of prior pelvic surgery.

Transverse transabdominal ultrasound in a patient undergoing fertility treatment demonstrates a massively enlarged right ovary ﬆ containing several large follicles. Note the size of the ovary compared to the adjacent uterus ﬅ. A large volume of pelvic ascites ﬇ is present.
Transverse transabdominal ultrasound in the same patient demonstrates enlargement of the left ovary ﬆ as well, which also contains several large follicles. Note the pelvic ascites ﬇.

Transverse transabdominal ultrasound in a patient undergoing fertility treatment demonstrates an enlarged right ovary ﬆ, measuring > 7 cm in length, and containing multiple large follicles. The left ovary had a similar appearance.

Transverse duplex Doppler ultrasound in the same patient demonstrates a low-resistance ovarian arterial waveform upon spectral evaluation, a typical finding in moderate or severe ovarian hyperstimulation.

Transverse transvaginal ultrasound in a patient undergoing fertility treatment shows an abnormally enlarged right ovary ﬆ, measuring 7.5 cm in length. The ovary is largely replaced by follicles ﬅ and demonstrates a classic wheel-spoke appearance. Note the adjacent pelvic ascites ﬇.

Transverse transvaginal ultrasound in the same patient demonstrates a similar appearance to the left ovary ﬆ. Ascites is noted as well ﬇. This patient met diagnostic criteria for ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome.

Axial transabdominal color Doppler US in a patient with a hydatidiform mole shows an enlarged ovary ﬅ (10 cm in length) containing multiple simple-appearing cysts. Normal venous waveform is seen in the intervening ovarian stroma. The ovarian cysts completely resolved on a follow-up ultrasound performed 1 month after evacuation of the molar pregnancy.

Axial transabdominal US in a 28-year-old woman with a diagnosis of gestational trophoblastic neoplasia (GTN) shows an enlarged ovary ﬅ composed of numerous different-sized simple cysts. These are individual cysts separated by residual ovarian tissue ﬇ rather than true septations, as seen in ovarian epithelial neoplasms.
Sagittal transvaginal US in a 25-year-old pregnant woman with twin gestations shows an enlarged ovary ﬅ composed of numerous different-sized simple cysts separated by thin septations.
Transverse transvaginal ultrasound of the left ovary ﬈ shows multiple peripherally located follicles ﬇ with a total volume of 14 mL.

Longitudinal pulsed Doppler ultrasound of the right ovary in the same patient shows an enlarged ovary with a volume of 27-mL peripherally displaced follicles. Stromal blood flow is characteristically increased, while resistive index is decreased in this patient with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS).
Transverse transvaginal ultrasound shows an enlarged left ovary ﬆ with multiple small, peripheral follicles ﬅ and a prominent, echogenic central stroma.

Transverse transvaginal ultrasound in the same patient shows an enlarged right ovary ﬅ with hypertrophic central stroma and peripherally displaced small follicles ﬇. Despite high-resolution imaging with an 8-MHz transducer, many of the small follicles cannot be resolved to allow an accurate count.

Transvaginal ultrasound shows an enlarged right ovary ﬆ with subcapsular hypoechogenicity ﬅ, likely representing numerous small follicles. However, due to the use of a 6-MHz transducer, only a few distinct follicles ﬇ can be resolved. Ovarian volume was used to diagnose PCOS in this case due to inability to perform accurate follicle counts.
Transvaginal ultrasound in the same patient shows cystic endometrial thickening ﬅ, which can be due to prolonged proliferative-phase endometrium or hyperplasia.

Transverse transvaginal ultrasound demonstrates a complex left pelvic mass ﬅ with a linear internal echogenic septation ﬇. The left ovary ﬆ was positioned at the margin of the mass.

Transvaginal US in a young woman with pelvic pain shows an enlarged ovary (volume: 42 cm³). The central stroma is heterogeneous with peripheral displacement of small follicles ﬇.

Transvaginal transverse ultrasound shows an anechoic, simple-appearing cyst ﬅ adjacent to, but separate from, the left ovary ﬇.
Transverse transabdominal ultrasound shows an anechoic, unilocular cyst ﬅ adjacent to, but separate from, the right ovary ﬇.
